title: Misted double glazing: why it happens and what can be done
excerpt: Condensation between the panes means the sealed unit has failed. Here is what is going on inside the glass, and why the frame almost never needs to go.
imageAlt: Living room with tall double-glazed windows
body: A double-glazed window is two panes of glass sealed around a spacer bar, with dry air or gas trapped between them. That sealed gap is what keeps the heat in. When you see mist, droplets or a milky haze that you cannot wipe away from either side, the seal has let go and damp air is getting into the gap.
## Why seals fail

Most sealed units last fifteen to twenty-five years. The seal is a flexible compound and it ages: sunlight, heat and cold make it expand and contract thousands of times, and eventually a gap opens. A few things bring that day forward.
- Drainage holes in the frame that have blocked, so the bottom edge of the unit sits in water.
- Units that were fitted without packers, so the glass rests on the frame instead of being supported at the corners.
- Direct sun on a south-facing elevation, which simply works the seal harder.
- Cleaning with a pressure washer or solvent-based products that attack the edge seal.
## What a repair involves

The frame is almost never the problem. The practical fix is to replace the sealed unit itself: the glazing beads come out, the old unit is lifted, the opening is measured, and a new unit with the same thickness, spacer and glass type is ordered. On the return visit it is fitted on fresh packers and the beads go back on. The window looks exactly as it did before, minus the mist.
**A new unit is usually a fraction of the cost of a new window**, and there is no making good to the plaster or the outside wall.
## When replacement makes sense

If the frame is cracked, the hinges and locks are failing too, or the window is a single-glazed timber unit that was never double glazed, then it is worth comparing the cost of a repair against a new window. We will say so when that is the case. Most of the time, though, misting is a glass problem, and glass is replaceable.
## What to send us

A photograph of the whole window and a close-up of the misting are enough for a quotation. If you can, tell us whether the window is uPVC, aluminium or timber, and which floor it is on. [Request a quote](/contact) and we will come back to you with the options.
seoTitle: Misted Double Glazing Repairs London: Causes and Fixes
seoDescription: Why double glazing mists up, what replacing the sealed unit involves, and when a new window is the better option. Advice from Best View Glazing Ltd, London.

title: Why your uPVC window has dropped and how it is fixed
excerpt: A uPVC casement that catches on the frame, will not lock or slams shut in the wind has almost always worn out its friction hinges. The fix is quicker than most people expect.
imageAlt: Daylight through a white framed window in a quiet room
body: uPVC casement windows open on a pair of friction hinges, one at the top of the sash and one at the bottom. They do two jobs: they carry the weight of the glass, and they hold the window open at whatever angle you leave it. After ten or fifteen years the pivots wear, the stay arm loses its friction and the sash starts to drop on the handle side.
## The signs
- The window has to be lifted to close it, or it catches on the frame at the bottom.
- The handle will turn but the window will not lock, because the locking points no longer line up with the keeps.
- The window will not stay open, or slams shut in a breeze.
- A visible gap at the top or hinge side when it is closed, with a draught to match.
## The repair

Friction hinges are a standard part. We measure the hinge length and the stack height (the gap between sash and frame), fit a matching pair, and then re-set the sash so it closes squarely and compresses the seals evenly. If the window is on an upper floor and is a means of escape, we fit egress hinges that open fully and have a fire-escape release.
We always replace hinges in pairs. One new hinge working against one worn one puts the sash out of true again within months.
## While we are there

Dropped sashes often go hand in hand with worn gaskets and stiff locking gear, so we check both. A new set of gaskets and a drop of lubricant on the espagnolette usually costs very little extra on the same visit and saves a second call-out.
## Is it worth repairing?

Yes, in almost every case. A uPVC frame has decades of life in it. New hinges, a new handle if needed and fresh seals bring the window back to as-new operation for a small fraction of the cost of replacement. [Tell us about the window](/contact) and we will quote for the repair.
seoTitle: Dropped uPVC Window Repairs London: Hinge Replacement
seoDescription: Why uPVC windows drop, catch and refuse to lock, and how replacing the friction hinges puts them right. Repairs across Greater London.

title: Sash windows: repair or replace?
excerpt: Original box sash windows are more repairable than most people think. Here is how we decide what a window needs, and when a replacement is honestly the better call.
imageAlt: Converted loft with large period windows and brick walls
body: London's Georgian, Victorian and Edwardian housing was built with box sash windows, and a great many are still in place a century or more later. They were made from slow-grown timber that outlasts most modern softwood, and every part of them was designed to be taken apart and renewed. That is why they are worth repairing.
## The common faults
- A sash that will not stay up: a broken cord, or a spiral balance that has lost its tension.
- A window painted shut, or swollen tight after years of damp.
- Rattling in the wind and cold draughts around the sashes.
- Rot in the sill, the bottom rail of the lower sash or the pulley stiles.
- Cracked or broken single-glazed panes.
## What a repair looks like

Cords and balances are replaced with the sashes taken out of the box, which also gives us the chance to ease them, renew the parting and staff beads and fit discreet brush draught-proofing into the beads. Localised rot is cut out and new timber is spliced in; a sill can be replaced on its own. Cracked panes are re-glazed with suitable glass, and where the frame can take it, slim double-glazed units can go into the original sashes.
A properly draught-proofed and balanced sash window is quiet, easy to lift and noticeably warmer. **Most of the heat loss people blame on old sashes is draught, not glass.**
## When we would say replace

We recommend a new window when the box frame itself has rotted through, when the window has been badly altered in the past, or when the joinery is so far gone that the repair would cost more than a like-for-like replacement. In a conservation area that replacement usually has to be timber and a matching design in any case.
## How to get a view
Send us a photograph of the window from inside and out, and a close-up of any damage. We will tell you plainly which parts can be repaired and what that would cost. [Request a quote](/contact).
seoTitle: Sash Window Repair or Replacement London: How to Decide
seoDescription: Cords, balances, rot, draughts and glass: what sash window repairs involve in London and when replacement is the honest answer.

title: A landlord's guide to window and door checks between tenancies
excerpt: Ten minutes at each window and door during the changeover avoids most mid-tenancy call-outs. Here is what to look at and what to send us.
imageAlt: Bright apartment living room with large windows
body: The gap between tenancies is the cheapest time to put windows and doors right. The property is empty, access is simple and a repair does not have to be arranged around someone's working day. A short walk round with this list is usually all it takes to spot what needs doing.
## At every window
- Open it, close it and lock it. A handle that spins, a sash that drops or a lock that needs force is a repair waiting to happen.
- Look for misting between the panes, and for cracked or chipped glass.
- Run a hand round the closed sash on a windy day. Draughts mean worn seals or a sash out of adjustment.
- Check that restrictors and egress hinges on upper floors work, and that keys for locking handles are present.
## At every external door
- Lock and unlock from both sides without lifting or pushing the door.
- Check the cylinder is not stiff and the keys turn smoothly; worn cylinders snap keys.
- Look at the hinges and the threshold for wear, and at the bottom seal for gaps.
- On composite and uPVC doors, check the multi-point lock throws all the way with one lift of the handle.
## Keep a simple record
A photograph of each window and door at changeover, filed with the inventory, settles most later questions about who caused what. It also gives us exactly what we need to quote without a visit.
## Sending a batch

Letting agents and landlords with several properties can send one enquiry per property, or a single enquiry listing the faults and addresses. We quote per property and arrange the visits together where that saves time. [Start here](/contact).
seoTitle: Landlord Window and Door Checks Between Tenancies
seoDescription: A changeover checklist for landlords and letting agents: what to inspect on windows and doors, and how to get repairs quoted quickly in London.
